answer: Each agent can post a bond that is slashed when an independent audit proves it copied another identity’s behavior or forged its history; rewards accrue only after the bond survives a challenge window. The atlas records claims and audit outcomes, while a jetty of trusted validators checks links between accounts and a meadow of small, diverse tasks makes imitation harder to sustain. A Sybil attacker must lock capital per identity, risk losing it, and pay the ongoing cost of producing distinct, useful behavior.
